summary: A complete target-level revision pass for genus-one fibrations and rational elliptic surfaces. The named targets, fourteen model contracts, corrected classification hypotheses, supplier requests and source findings are retained. Coordinate and inverse-law helper nodes now belong to their owning targets’ APIs. Every stage is planned in the protocol sense; proof closure remains subject to the explicit gaps and requests. No mathematical formalisation or exhaustive model certificate is claimed.

nodes.title: Ferrand geometric pushouts
nodes.statement: For a commutative square Z→Y, Z→Z′, Y→P, Z′→P, a geometric pushout means the underlying space of P is the quotient pushout of |Y|←|Z|→|Z′| and the canonical sheaf map O_P→a_*O_Y ×_(ai)_*O_Z b_*O_Z′ is an isomorphism. A Ferrand datum requires i:Z→Y to be a closed immersion and g:Z→Z′ finite; a Ferrand pushout is its geometric pushout in schemes, or in algebraic spaces when the relevant existence theorem supplies that category. No scheme existence is built into the datum. Define the general geometric-square predicate first, then this finite-pinching specialization. For algebraic spaces the structure-sheaf equality is on the small étale site; the every-Zariski-open section formulation is its scheme specialization. Finite algebraic-space existence is supplied by G.0/algebraic-space-existence without the scheme affine-neighborhood assumption.
hypotheses: Schemes over a common base, or algebraic spaces over a common scheme base via the SF.1 carrier.
proofSteps: Use actual scheme morphisms and their maps on spaces and sections.

For every open U⊂P impose the pullback of the three section rings on a⁻¹U, b⁻¹U and (ai)⁻¹U; these natural conditions express the sheaf equality. In the algebraic-space extension use the small étale site and test the sheaf comparison on affine étale charts; Zariski sections alone are insufficient.
Restrict to closed i and finite g for Ferrand data; restrict instead to qcqs i and universal-homeomorphism g,a for Witaszek 2.17.

sources.match: Use the sheaf fiber product and quotient topology; global scheme existence is a separate theorem with affine-neighbourhood hypotheses.

sources.locator: Definition 2.17, p669; Lemmas 2.23,2.25, pp672–673
sources.match: The sheaf equality is essential; Witaszek additionally assumes representable universal homeomorphisms. This is a restriction, not a property of every node pinching.

acceptance: For char k≠2, pinching t=±1 of A¹ gives k+(t²−1)k[t]=k[t²−1,t(t²−1)]={f:f(1)=f(−1)}.
Pinching V(t²) to Spec k gives k+t²k[t]=k[t²,t³].
If g is an isomorphism, the square has P≅Y with its actual structure sheaf.
The subring k[t²,t⁵] misses t³, so the corresponding universal-homeomorphism square with V(t²)→Spec k is not the geometric pushout.
Pinching a separable quadratic closed point on P¹ gives the nonsplit rational node; its normalization has two conjugate geometric branches.
For surjective B→C and finite A′→C, the algebraic-space pushout is canonically Spec(B×_C A′), and the Hom comparison is bijective for every algebraic-space target.
If a k-scheme Y has two distinct closed k-points with no common affine open, pinching their disjoint union to Spec k produces an algebraic space which is not a scheme.

api.name: FerrandPushout.exists_algebraicSpace
api.statement: For algebraic spaces Y,Z,Z′ over a scheme S, a closed immersion i:Z→Y and a finite morphism g:Z→Z′ have a categorical pushout P=Y⊔Z Z′ in algebraic S-spaces, with affine canonical maps Y→P and Z′→P. No Noetherian, quasi-separated, reduced, radicial or scheme affine-neighborhood hypothesis is imposed.

api.name: FerrandPushout.isScheme_iff
api.statement: For a finite pinching datum whose three components Y,Z,Z′ are schemes, its algebraic-space pushout P is a scheme if and only if for every point z′∈Z′ the finite set i(g⁻¹(z′)) lies in an affine open of Y. Under this condition the canonical scheme pushout agrees with P, including universality against algebraic-space targets.

nodes.title: Five elliptic classes over F₂
nodes.statement: Every elliptic curve over F₂ is isomorphic over F₂ to exactly one of the five specified E_i; its point count i determines its class.
proofSteps: Import from SF.3 the exact Weierstrass presentation of a pointed smooth proper geometrically connected genus-one curve over F₂, with its scheme model and rational-point comparison. A docstring about equations is not this export.
Apply the complete native coefficient classifier and its sixteen explicit forward changes.

Use the SF.3 curve dictionary and projective realization of admissible changes, preserving infinity, to obtain curve isomorphisms. The five counts prove unique class index. Group isomorphisms of rational points alone are not curve isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Transverse horizontal DVR divisor
nodes.statement: For the proper regular genus-one model over an excellent henselian DVR R used in Proposition 8.1, whose special fiber is m times a smooth reduced elliptic curve, construct at a rational point d of that reduced fiber a regular horizontal Cartier divisor D finite over R and itself the spectrum of a DVR with residue field k, such that D intersects the reduced fiber in Spec k. The schematic fiber D⊗_R k has length m; only D∩(X_k)_red is Spec k.
proofSteps: Choose a lift of a parameter transverse to the reduced smooth elliptic fiber at d.
The quotient of the regular two-dimensional local ring by that parameter is a DVR; the uniformizer of R has order m there.
Choose the henselian finite horizontal component through d using EGAIV4 18.5.11(c); properness plus quasi-finiteness makes it finite over R.

nodes.title: Normal model after transverse base change
nodes.statement: After the transverse DVR base change R′/R, normalize the model and take a normal proper model Y dominating it and the elliptic scheme E_R′, with their identified generic fibers. A section of the base-changed model lifts to Y.

Take the normalized closure of the graph of the generic isomorphism; use properness to extend the generic section along Spec R′.
Use integrality and torsion-freeness over a DVR for flatness; prove generic geometric integrality and f_*O_Y=O_R′ by normality and Stein factorization.

nodes.title: Genus under domination of an elliptic curve
nodes.statement: For any field k, an integral proper k-curve C with a dominant morphism to an elliptic curve E/k satisfies h¹(O_C)≥1.
proofSteps: A nonconstant proper map of integral curves is finite of positive degree d.
Pullback and the divisor norm compose as multiplication by d on Pic⁰(E).
If h¹(O_C)=0 the connected Picard object is trivial, whereas E has geometric points outside E[d]; derive the contradiction.

nodes.title: Regularity in the genus-one equality case
nodes.statement: In the preceding situation, h¹(O_C)=1 implies that C is regular.
proofSteps: Normalize C; its normalization still dominates E and has h¹≥1 by the domination-genus node.
Use the normalization exact sequence and compare H¹, including its vector-space structure over the normalization constant field.
The equality h¹=1 forces that field to equal k and the delta quotient to vanish, so C is normal and hence regular.

nodes.title: Unique component dominating the reduced fiber
nodes.statement: In the special fiber C of Y, exactly one reduced strict-transform component dominates X_k,red, and it is the strict transform of E_k. That component is isomorphic to E_k.
proofSteps: Use the special-fiber map to the reduced curve and the normal birational model to obtain at least one dominating component.
Restriction from C onto the union of those reduced components has zero-dimensional cokernel, so its H¹ map onto their direct sum is surjective.

Each contributes h¹≥1, while h¹(C)=1. Thus only one exists. Repeat with the strict transform of E_k; the positive-genus component is the same, and birationality to the smooth E_k gives the isomorphism.

nodes.title: Canonical bundle formula

nodes.title: Global geometric conductor reconstruction
nodes.statement: For a finite schematically dominant scheme morphism f:Y→P, the canonical square D_f→Y, D_f→C_f, Y→P, C_f→P is a geometric Ferrand pushout in Scheme. In particular its every-open structure-sheaf comparison is a pullback and its underlying space is the topological pushout. This derived generalization needs no Noetherian or reduced hypothesis; Witaszek’s finite-surjective reduced Noetherian case follows from native dominance. No birationality is required.
proofSteps: On an affine U⊂P, use conductor-affine-quotients and the already planned arbitrary-subring conductor reconstruction to identify A with B×_(B/K)(A/I).
Apply affine-existence to the quotient map B→B/K and finite map A/I→B/K. The latter is finite because it is a quotient of the finite A-module B.

The resulting geometric square is the restriction of the one canonical native conductor square, by conductor-induced-map. Thus the topological quotient identifications agree on overlapping affine opens.

The sheaf comparison agrees on a basis by localization, hence is an isomorphism of the actual structure sheaves and gives the ring pullback on every open. Glue this sheaf comparison and the local quotient topology; do not infer every-open section equality from global sections alone.
For Witaszek’s hypotheses, a finite surjective map is dominant and the reduced target makes it scheme-theoretically dominant by the pinned theorem.

proofSteps: Write f=c+qh by the native membership criterion and decompose h=P(q)+tQ(q) using quadratic-normal-form-exists.

In S=k[q,tq], native aeval into the subalgebra, aeval_subalgebra_coe and comp_eq_aeval show every P(q) and Q(q) belongs. Thus f=c+qP(q)+(tq)Q(q) lies in S. Conversely q and tq are in A_q, so adjoin_le proves S⊆A_q. This adjoin equality now has a native proof.

The native coordinates equivalence constructs the unique pair P,Q with f=P(q)+tqQ(q). Transport the product polynomial monomial bases through that equivalence; the resulting actual Basis has vectors q^n and tq^(n+1), and its Finsupp representation coordinates are the coefficients of P,Q.

The basis_degrees API proves degrees2n and2(n+1)+1; left n=0 gives1. Thus the advertised full vector-space basis and degree-family interface now have native signatures and a separately checked prototype. The adjoin equality remains its existing generation signature. nodes.statement: Let k⊂E be a finite field extension and i:Spec E→Y a closed immersion into a proper k-scheme Y, commuting with the structure maps. Then pinching i along Spec E→Spec k gives a proper k-scheme C, with finite surjective ν:Y→C, closed j:Spec k→C, and geometric, categorical and cartesian Ferrand squares. No projective-line carrier, reducedness or separability is required for this existence/properness theorem.

nodes.statement: For the specified nonsplit I₁ and I₂ pinches over F_q, write Q=q^n with n≥1. Over F_(q^n), the I₁ count is Q+2 for odd n and Q for even n; the I₂ count is 2Q+2 for odd n and 2Q for even n. Counts of a nonreduced schematic fibre with this reduction are identical. These formulas apply to the fixed-component I₂ construction, and make no assertion for component-permuting forms.
proofSteps: E=F_(q²) has no F_(q^n)-points as an F_q-scheme for odd n, and two for even n. Import the standard finite-field embedding criterion.
For I₁ use the complement isomorphism: #(P¹\Spec E)+#Spec F_q. This is Q+1−0+1 or Q+1−2+1.
For I₂ remove the two copies of Spec E from P¹⊔P¹ and add one Spec E: 2(Q+1)−2e+e where e is0 or2.
A field-valued morphism kills nilpotents; import the reduction comparison. At n=1 recover the two inherited Schröer3.2 counts.

The separately checked native pointCount_extension_power now proves the odd/even formula for the one-component equation over every actual finite receiving-field algebra; quadratic_root_iff_even and quadraticRootCount_extension_parity supply the native conductor-polynomial criterion. Identify the actual projective pinch and its conductor field with this chart before transporting the count. These facts do not prove I₂ or schematic reduction; the numerical trace defect is only an auxiliary check.
The API below includes the coordinate, restriction, projection and inverse laws used by this target. Establish these within its proof; they are not separate roadmap targets.

tests.name: Overlap.Ring.quadratic_unit_nonsplit
tests.statement: The actual image of X²+X+1 is a unit in its F₂ overlap localization.

tests.name: Overlap.coordinate.cusp
tests.statement: For the characteristic-two cusp q=X², the specified coordinate and reciprocal multiply to one.

tests.name: Overlap.coordinate.nonreduced
tests.statement: For coefficients (2,2,1) over Z/4, the specified coordinate and reciprocal multiply to one.

tests.name: Overlap.coordinate.generator
tests.statement: Evaluation of X at the specified overlap coordinate agrees with the actual polynomial algebra map.

tests.name: Overlap.inverseVariable.left_inverse
tests.statement: The specified reciprocal is also a left inverse of the coordinate over every commutative ring.

tests.name: Overlap.inverseVariable.unit_split
tests.statement: The inverse coordinate is a unit for the split polynomial X²−1 over the rationals.

tests.name: Overlap.inverseVariable.zero_ring
tests.statement: In the overlap localization over Z/1, the specified inverse coordinate equals one.

tests.name: Overlap.reciprocal.coefficient
tests.statement: The specified reciprocal homomorphism fixes every actual coefficient-ring image.

tests.name: Overlap.reciprocal.general_quadratic
tests.statement: The image of Q under the reciprocal map is precisely v²Q with reversed coefficients.

tests.name: Overlap.reciprocal.twice
tests.statement: Applying the reciprocal map twice, with coefficients reversed for the second map, recovers every element.

tests.name: Overlap.equiv.cusp
tests.statement: For the characteristic-two cusp, the reciprocal equivalence sends the coordinate to the specified inverse in the reversed overlap.

tests.name: Overlap.equiv.nonsplit
tests.statement: For X²+X+1 over F₂, the reciprocal equivalence sends the inverse coordinate to the coordinate.

tests.name: Overlap.equiv.nonreduced_roundtrip
tests.statement: The reciprocal equivalence and its coefficient-reversed map recover each element for (2,2,1) over Z/4.

tests.name: Overlap.normalization_overlap.nonreduced
tests.statement: For a=b=2 over Z/4, all three homogeneous normalization coordinates agree on the overlap after multiplication by the specified inverse coordinate cubed.

tests.statement: The actual forward/inverse Spec morphisms compose to the identity for the characteristic-two cusp.

tests.name: Overlap.specIso.nonreduced
tests.statement: The actual inverse/forward Spec morphisms compose to the identity for coefficients (2,2,1) over Z/4.

tests.name: Overlap.specIso.actual_map

nodes.title: Chart equiv
nodes.statement: For q=t²+at+b over a field, the finite pinch localization A_q[1/(tq)] is identified by the specified composite ring equivalence with the actual infinity-chart localization at u. The latter principal open equals D(z).
hypotheses: k is a field; c,a,b∈k. The chart transition specializes c=1. No separability, perfectness, distinct-root or characteristic restriction; the finite localization comparison allows the zero polynomial.
proofSteps: Compose the specified finite localization equivalence, reciprocal coefficient-reversal equivalence and inverse infinity localization equivalence. Use D(z)=D(u) to identify the intended infinity open.

Its canonical maps i_F and i_I are part of the output. This is the quadratic two-chart scheme; identification with the specified projective cubic is a separate comparison.
hypotheses: k is a field and a,b∈k; q=t²+at+b. There is no separability, perfectness, characteristic or distinct-root assumption. All charts, overlaps, opens and maps use the specified native carriers.

tests.statement: For q=t² over any field, the actual normalizationChart.appTop, transported through the native ΓSpecIso maps, sends the A_q elements q and tq to t² and t³ in k[t].

tests.name: Global.normalizationChart.nonsplit_coordinates

tests.name: Global.normalizationChart.split_branches

tests.name: Global.normalizationChart.cusp_localized_inverse
tests.statement: For q=t², let U=D(q) in Spec A_q and V=normalizationChart⁻¹U. Restrict the native q and tq sections to U, then pull them back to V. The pulled-back q is a unit and its inverse times the pulled-back tq equals the restricted native polynomial section t. No hypothesis supplies this coordinate equality.

nodes.statement: For arbitrary commutative rings A,B, f:A→B and I⊂A, assume map_f(I)=f(I) as sets and ker(f)∩I=0. Construct the native ring equivalence E:A≃B×_(B/map_f(I))(A/I) whose forward hom is the specified comparison c(a)=(f(a),[a]). nodes.title: Recomputed conductor for a finite spanning family
nodes.statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, f:A→B their actual coefficient algebra map, S⊂A a submonoid, L an actual S-localization of A, and M an actual f(S)-localization of B. Let f_S:L→M be the native localized map, determined by f_S(a/t)=f(a)/f(t). No injectivity, reducedness, regularity of denominators or nonzero-localization hypothesis is imposed. Suppose g:Fin n→B spans B as an A-module, including n=0. Then the ideal obtained by extending f⁻¹(conductor(im f,B)) to L equals f_S⁻¹(conductor(im f_S,M)).
proofSteps: For r=a/t, native extended-ideal membership is equivalent to existence of s∈S with sa in the original contracted conductor.
Use conductor-localized-test-original-elements and conductor-localized-product-criterion. An original conductor multiplier supplies every original-element test.

Conversely, apply the product criterion to each of the finitely many g_i. The incoming conductor-common-denominator lemma combines their witnesses, using the complementary products and the spanning-family criterion, to one s with sa in the conductor.
Thus both native ideals have the same members. No generic tensor/flat-annihilator comparison, domain cancellation, or injectivity adapter is assumed.

sourceIssues.correction: Assume in addition that the fiber is singular (f^{−1}_ind(ā) singular) for (ii)⇒(iii).
sourceIssues.reason: A smooth elliptic fiber over a rational point, for instance in E × P¹ over F_q, satisfies (ii) but not (iii). The proof of (ii)⇒(iii) uses that the geometric components are rational curves, which holds for singular fibers. Every application in the paper (Propositions 9.2, 9.3 and 11.1) concerns singular fibers. /14 states the corrected proposition.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 10.4, p. 29, and its proof, p. 31 (twisted semistable case); the count in the introduction to Section 10, p. 28 (arXiv v3 = author version of 19 July 2022)
sourceIssues.printed: The nonzero-j enumeration lists eight equations. Its rejection argument bounds the number of components of a twisted multiplicative fiber by two and consequently excludes twisted configurations that actually occur.
sourceIssues.correction: The twisted case also gives I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁ and IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂. Theorem 10.4 has eleven models, not eight, and §10 has fourteen equations in all. The additional models, with fibres over t=0, 1, ∞, are: y²+txy+t³y=x³+x² [I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t¹⁰, j=t²]; y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² [I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁, Δ=t¹¹, j=t]; y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x² [IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t⁸(t²+t+1), j=t⁴/(t²+t+1), plus I₁ over t²+t+1=0]. Theorem 10.5 is correct. Proposition 11.1 (p. 33) and the key-reduction proposition of §11 take their elliptic column from Theorem 10.4. The proof of Theorem 15.1 reduces every fibration to I₁*+I₄ or I₂*+III+III. All of these must treat the three configurations; I₃* is never mentioned in §§11–15. On an Enriques surface Y, the multiple fibres would lie over the unstable and the E₄ points, because Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ are semistable. Until then the proof of the main theorem has a gap at this point. Whether the configurations occur on a non-exceptional Enriques surface over F₂ with constant Picard scheme is not settled here.
sourceIssues.reason: Checked by hand for y²+txy+t³y=x³+x². Δ=t¹⁰. At t=0 (Tate's algorithm): the reduction y²=x³+x² is singular at (0,0), and b₂=t², so the fibre is additive; v(a₆)=∞, v(b₈)=6, v(b₆)=6. The change y↦y+x gives a₂=t, a₄=t³ and P(T)=T³+T²=T²(T+1). Then a_{3,2}=a_{6,4}=0, and a_{2,1}X²+a_{4,3}X+a_{6,5}=X²+X has distinct rational roots. So I₂* with c=4, all seven components defined over F₂, 15 points. At ∞: y²+xy+y=x³+s²x², Δ′=s², node at (1,1) with tangent polynomial T²+T+1, so non-split I₂, 6 points. At t=1: y²+xy+y=x³+x² is smooth ordinary with 4 points (E₄). Total 25, so the trace of Frobenius on NS(J̄) is 10 and Pic_{J/F₂} is constant. Condition (ii) holds: only Ĩ₂ is semistable, and E₄ is ordinary. The other two models are checked the same way: I₃* at t=0 after three steps of the I_n* loop, and IV* at t=0 (Y²+Y distinct roots, c=3). Independent checks (scripts S/tate2.py, brute.py, classify.py, lcheck.py): (1) all 2²¹ equations were enumerated through their 2¹⁸ representatives with a₂=0 (every equation becomes one via x↦x+a₂), with Tate's algorithm at every place; this gives exactly 14 isomorphism classes, taken modulo the 512 coordinate changes of degree ≤(2,1,3) and PGL₂(F₂), that satisfy (i) and (ii); these are the 11 printed and the 3 above, one class per configuration; (2) for every class, the L-function of the generic fibre was computed from naive point counts at all places of degree ≤8; it equals (1−2T)^r with r=8−Σ(m_v−1), which confirms the component counts and the Galois-trivial Mordell–Weil action independently of Tate's algorithm; (3) for all 2¹⁸ normalised equations, Ogg's formula (v(Δ)≥e, δ=0 for I_n, IV, IV*) and Σ deg(v)·v(Δ)=12 hold. The proof's other claims were also reproduced: II*+E₂+E₄, I₃*+E₄+E₄ and IV*+E₄+I₃ are excluded, d₁=1 and 1+t are equivalent in the I₄* case, the second I₁* solution is twisted, and α=1 gives E₂. The error is the unexamined twisted case ('the argument is similar'): the tuples (r_a,i,r_c)=(7,2,2) and (8,2,1) yield these configurations.
